summary: Heather Cooper prompted Claude Opus 5.5 to independently create a motion piece showcasing its capabilities. Working autonomously over 97 minutes, Opus generated an entire motion sequence and accompanying sound through pure code, featuring geometric progressions, GLSL refraction shaders, physics simulations, an 8,192-boid flocking simulation, and procedural geography.
summaryEn: Full Stop: Autonomous Creative Coding Showcase by Claude Opus 5.5

post.originalText:
I asked Claude Opus 5.5 (Max) this prompt:

"Create me a motion video of your choice, with the sole purpose of flexing Opus 5.5 capabilities."

It worked on its own for 1 hour 37 minutes and gave me this:

→ @claudeai https://t.co/HdwYh039In

sourceMaterials.text: @Art_For_Joy @claudeai Yeah, I'm glad he's back home because it was so weird without any of them here! No renovations anytime soon, but it's very helpful to have him here to plan and handle little emergencies or small upgrades (he installed a new closet organizer system in a walk-in closet yesterday) 🥰
sourceMaterials.author: HBCoop_

sourceMaterials.text: @Art_For_Joy @claudeai Thank you! Luckily, the eldest child moved back home after he graduated a couple of years ago, so we aren't empty nesters yet - he's a construction manager and hopefully he can handle home renovations when I'm ready 😂
sourceMaterials.author: HBCoop_

sourceMaterials.text: @gen_ericai @claudeai It is and I'm constantly surprised ☺️
sourceMaterials.author: HBCoop_

sourceMaterials.text:
@Art_For_Joy @claudeai Thanks Art! It is wild how much we can do now! 

It's good to see you! We're doing well (my babies are college freshmen now, so that feels pretty crazy) 😅 Hope you and your family are doing well 🤗
sourceMaterials.author: HBCoop_

sourceMaterials.text: @CoffeeVectors @claudeai It's crazy how it jumped to this level so quickly
sourceMaterials.author: HBCoop_

sourceMaterials.text: Every frame and every sound is code, with no video model or music generator. The flock is 8,192 simulated birds. Claude typed the coastlines in from memory, and the glass ball sits on the code that draws it. For a second after the ball opens, the birds come out as a clump before they find their shape.
